The answer is C, about -40%. Southern approval of school desegregation was far below approval in the rest of the U.S., so South minus rest of U.S. is negative. The gap was about 40 points at its widest, in the 1950s (roughly 15–20% in the South versus about 60% elsewhere). That also fits the team note that the answer is either -40% or -80%, since -80% would need near-zero Southern approval against near-universal approval elsewhere.

CONFIDENCE: 80
